The Department has issued a demand for TDS default amounting of INR 181.79 Mn for 8 years from FY 16 to FY 23. The Assessing Officer (TDS) has passed the Order Giving Effect (OGE) to the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Order vide dated 30th December 2025 for 7 years i.e., AY 2016- 17, AY 2018-19 to AY 2023-24. The final interest u/s 201(1A) for the said years amounted to INR 25,13,273/ - (restricted up to the date of actual payment of TDS) from the earlier TDS liability. (For details refer Stock Exchanges disclosure dated 8th November 2025 and 31st December 2025 respectively.)

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received an unfavourable order from CIT(A) for FY 16 and FY 18 to FY 23 (i.e. 7 years) amounting to INR 170.41 mn. The IT Department had considered company as assessee in default for not deducting TDS on year end provisions for expenses which company already disallowed as per section 40(a)(ia) in their respective year's computation of Income. The Department has issued a demand for TDS default amounting of INR 181.79 Mn for 8 years from FY 16 to FY 23. While issuing the order, the IT Department did not consider subsequent deduction of TDS while making payment to vendors. The Company has filed an appeal against the impugned order with Tribunal (ITAT). The ITAT, Mumbai, vide its order dated 7th November 2025, held that the Company cannot be treated as an “assessee in default” under Section 201(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, where the underlying tax has been subsequently deducted and deposited. The ITAT further held that interest under Section 201(1A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 shall be restricted upto the date of actual payment of such taxes. Pursuant to the aforesaid order, the Assistant Commissioner of Income-Tax (TDS) had passed an order giving effect to the ITAT ruling and has raised a demand towards interest under Section 201(1A) of the IncomeTax Act, 1961 amounting to INR 2.51 million, as against the original demand of INR 170.41 million.
tax_litigation.status: Income-Tax (TDS) Department has filed an appeal u/s 260A of Income Tax Act, 1961 before the Hon’ble Bombay High Court challenging the order passed by the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) in favour of the Company. The appeal pertains to AY 2016–17, AY 2018–19 to 2023–24.

timeline.summary: Sapphire Foods Mauritius Limited’s promoter **Faatimah Khodadeen** declared no new encumbrances on Sapphire Foods India shares as of **April 2, 2026**, beyond prior disclosures.
Sapphire Foods received approval from Hon'ble Regional Director to shift registered office from Maharashtra to Haryana on 21st April 2026
Sapphire Foods reported that the Income-Tax TDS department appealed in the Bombay High Court against a favorable ITAT ruling, with the disputed interest demand reduced to ₹0.25 Cr.
Sapphire Foods reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹789.8 Cr, up 11% YoY, driven by strong KFC consumer recruitment and 19 new restaurant additions.
SACHIN Dudam (Chairman) shared the Q4 FY26 earnings call recording on 28 April 2026 via the company’s investor relations website.
Sapphire Foods published its corporate presentation for Q4 FY26, highlighting a network of 1,052 restaurants and ₹790 Cr in restaurant sales.
Sapphire Foods reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹792.22 Cr, up 11% YoY, with KFC SSSG at 4% and continuing store expansions.
Sapphire Foods received two Tamil Nadu GST show cause notices dated 26 May 2026 alleging excess input tax credit of ₹977.06 million (₹97.7 Cr) for FY23 and FY24, which it calls not maintainable.
Sapphire Foods reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹888 Cr and a net loss of ₹1.51 Cr, while progressing its merger with Devyani International.
Sapphire Foods reported Q2FY27 revenue up 20% YoY to ₹885.34 Cr with KFC SSSG of 14% and total restaurant count reaching 1,086.
Sachin Dudam (Chairman) shared Q2 & H1 FY27 earnings call recording on 22 Oct 2026 via Sapphire Foods’ investor relations website.
Sapphire Foods reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹885 Cr up 20% YoY and adjusted EBITDA of ₹62.4 Cr up 39% YoY, driven by strong transaction growth.
Sapphire Foods received Competition Commission of India approval for its proposed merger with Devyani International.
